clue.text: Over-excited drunk

blocks.note: first meaning: elated, wound up, euphoric
second meaning: intoxicated, under the influence

explanation.walkthrough: The two words read as one description of a rowdy reveller, but each is a separate meaning of the same short word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes both a state of feverish elation and the condition of someone intoxicated by drink or drugs.

clue.text: A port much favoured round pub

indicators.note: one piece goes round another, wrapping it on both sides

blocks.note: a hot favourite is the one most fancied to win
a bar is a place to drink

explanation.surface: A sailor's favourite harbour town, beloved for the pub nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Much favoured' points to a hot favourite, the runner everyone backs; 'A port' is the whole definition, not a separate article.
explanation.definitionFit: Hobart is the harbour capital of Tasmania, so it is an example of a port.

clue.text: Beef, excellent in New Zealand

blocks.note: first meaning: a complaint or grumble, also the verb to grumble
second meaning: Australian and New Zealand slang for very good

explanation.walkthrough: Beef looks like meat praised by New Zealanders, but it is slang for a complaint. In Australian and New Zealand English the word is also an adjective meaning great.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun the word is a grievance (a beef), and in antipodean slang it is an adjective of high praise.

clue.text: Ascend, then leave drive

blocks.note: to get up is to rise or climb
and then: a joining word
to go is to depart

explanation.surface: Instructions for a journey: climb up, then set off by car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drive' looks like a car journey but is the noun for energy and ambition.
explanation.definitionFit: Get-up-and-go is an idiom for energetic enthusiasm, the same as drive in the sense of ambition.

clue.text: Former partner, frightfully urbane, left, finally, in high spirits

indicators.note: frightfully suggests something terribly disordered, so these letters are thrown about
finally points to the very end of the word before it, keeping only its closing letter

blocks.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner
letters to rearrange
its final letter

explanation.surface: A sophisticated ex walked out, and their former partner is overjoyed about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Exuberant means full of cheerful energy, a synonym for being in high spirits.

clue.text: Drug addicts employ extremes of recklessness

indicators.note: extremes are the two ends, so only the first and last letters of the next word are kept

blocks.note: to employ something is to use it
first and last letters

explanation.surface: Addicts take their drugs with reckless abandon at either end of the scale.
explanation.definitionFit: Users is everyday slang for people who habitually take illegal drugs, that is, addicts.

clue.text: Sexy looking girl? One to go astray in a resort — less on!

indicators.note: less means minus, so the word after it is subtracted from the place name
in places the opening pieces inside the shortened resort

blocks.note: taken as written
Brighton is a seaside resort on the English south coast
taken as written, to be removed
Roman numeral one
taken as written
to fall is to lapse morally, to go astray

explanation.surface: A seaside fling: a pretty girl goes off the rails at a resort, wearing very little.
explanation.walkthrough: The resort is Brighton, a seaside town south of London. 'Go astray' carries the old moral sense of falling from virtue.
explanation.definitionFit: A bit of all right is British slang for a sexually attractive person, so it fits a sexy-looking girl.

clue.text: Verbal onslaught from daughter, one with a large family

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter
Roman numeral one
a tribe is a large family group

explanation.surface: A tirade from a daughter who is one of many siblings.
explanation.definitionFit: A diatribe is a bitter spoken or written attack, which is a verbal onslaught.

clue.text: Plain old bicycle

blocks.note: first meaning: unremarkable, commonplace
second meaning: the high-wheeled penny-farthing, once known by this name

explanation.walkthrough: The penny-farthing, with its huge front wheel, was called an ordinary once the modern safety bicycle arrived.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means plain or unexceptional, and as a noun it is the historical name for a penny-farthing bike.

clue.text: Magic lantern may show lost soldier holding map out?

indicators.note: something lost has wandered off course, so these letters stray into a new order
holding means keeping inside, so the rearranged letters wrap around the other piece

blocks.note: letters to rearrange
to project is to map out or plan, and also to draw a map projection

explanation.surface: An old picture show depicting a stray soldier holding out his map.
explanation.walkthrough: The scene reads like the subject of a lantern slide; 'lost' looks descriptive but rearranges the soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: The magic lantern was the Victorian forerunner of the device that casts images from small transparencies onto a screen.

clue.text: One that devours the written word?

definitions.text: One that devours the written word?

blocks.clueFragment: One that devours the written word?
blocks.note: surface reading: a voracious reader, someone who gobbles up literature
setter's reading: a tiny insect that literally eats the paper and paste of books

explanation.walkthrough: It looks like a bookworm-type keen reader, but the eater here is a small wingless insect that feeds on old paper and binding glue.
explanation.definitionFit: This insect damages libraries by feeding on mould, paper and glue, so it literally consumes printed pages.

clue.text: Excellent week off in which to see chamois

indicators.note: off means removed, so that letter is taken away

blocks.note: wizard is British slang for excellent
W is the abbreviation for week

explanation.surface: A splendid week's holiday spent spotting mountain goats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wizard!' is old-fashioned British schoolboy slang for marvellous; drop W.
explanation.definitionFit: The izard is the Pyrenean chamois, a goat-antelope of the mountains between France and Spain.

clue.text: Form of rise appropriate for the remainder

indicators.note: a new form of a word reshapes its letters into a different order

blocks.note: letters to rearrange
what is due is fitting or proper

explanation.surface: A suitable rise in pay to cover what is left over.
explanation.definitionFit: A residue is what is left after the rest is removed, which is the remainder.

clue.text: Newly-designed apron's about right for Highlander's pouch

indicators.note: something newly designed has been remade, so these letters are rearranged
about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go round the other piece

blocks.note: letters to rearrange
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A redesigned apron is just right for a Scotsman's kit.
explanation.walkthrough: A Highlander is a Scot from the Highlands, who wears a kilt.
explanation.definitionFit: A sporran is the leather purse hung at the front of a Scottish kilt, a Highlander's pouch.

clue.text: Film polar bear swimming round mouth of huge river

indicators.note: swimming suggests moving about freely, so these letters drift into a new order
a mouth is an opening, so just the first letter is taken
round means encircling, so the rearranged letters go about one piece

blocks.note: letters to rearrange
R is the abbreviation for river, added to the rearranged letters
its first letter

explanation.surface: A wildlife film: a polar bear swims around the mouth of an enormous river.
explanation.walkthrough: POLAR BEAR plus R is rearranged and wrapped around H. The American spelling ARBOR is the film's title.
explanation.definitionFit: Pearl Harbor is the 2001 Hollywood war movie about the Japanese attack on the Hawaiian naval base.

clue.text: Dealing with one usually generates a lot of interest

definitions.text: Dealing with one usually generates a lot of interest

blocks.clueFragment: Dealing with one usually generates a lot of interest
blocks.note: surface reading: someone fascinating who attracts curiosity and attention
setter's reading: interest as the charge on borrowed money, which an illegal lender sets very high

explanation.walkthrough: 'Interest' suggests fascination, but it means the money a borrower pays back on top of the loan.
explanation.definitionFit: A predatory illegal moneylender charges exorbitant rates, so borrowing from one runs up a great deal of interest.

clue.text: Drab, short man in hat

indicators.note: short means cut off, so the name loses its final letter

blocks.note: sombre means dull or dark in colour
Ron is a man's name

explanation.surface: A dull little man wearing a hat.
explanation.walkthrough: RON is cut short to RO.
explanation.definitionFit: A sombrero is a broad-brimmed Mexican hat, so it is a particular kind of hat.

clue.text: Novelist from Maine, first to reach girl

indicators.note: first means the leading letter of the word that follows

blocks.note: ME is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Maine
its first letter
Edith is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A writer from Maine is the first to reach a girl.
explanation.definitionFit: George Meredith was a Victorian English novelist, author of The Egoist, so the surname names a writer of fiction.

clue.text: Wagon train route — looting rare, surprisingly

indicators.note: something that comes out surprisingly turns out unexpectedly, so these letters land in an unexpected order

blocks.note: letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: On the pioneers' wagon route, plundering was unusually uncommon.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oregon Trail was the nineteenth-century overland route followed by settlers' wagon trains to the American Northwest.

clue.text: A doctor, old Italian, is skilful

blocks.note: taken as written
Dr is the abbreviation for doctor
O is the abbreviation for old
It is the abbreviation for Italian

explanation.surface: An elderly Italian physician who is very capable.
explanation.definitionFit: Adroit means deft and clever with hands or mind, a synonym for skilful.

clue.text: A deadly sin, determined by common consent

blocks.note: taken as written
greed, or avarice, is one of the seven deadly sins

explanation.surface: Everyone agrees that one of the seven sins is bad.
explanation.definitionFit: Something agreed has been settled by everyone involved, that is, decided by mutual consent.

clue.text: Dictionary entry finally gives 'where beer is made'

indicators.note: finally points to the very end of the word before it, keeping only its closing letter

blocks.note: Brewer's Dictionary of Phrase and Fable is a famous reference work
its final letter

explanation.surface: A dictionary's last entry defines the place where beer is produced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dictionary' stands for Brewer's, the classic British reference book of phrase and fable.
explanation.definitionFit: A brewery is the plant or company that produces beer, the place where it is made.

clue.text: A short time on station over in Black Sea resort

indicators.note: over suggests turning things upside down, so in a down light the pieces read from the bottom up

blocks.note: taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time
to station is to place or set down, which is to lay

explanation.surface: A brief spell at a station before travelling on to a Black Sea seaside town.
explanation.definitionFit: Yalta is a resort city on the Crimean coast of the Black Sea, famous for the 1945 conference.

clue.text: Part of leg found by excavation causes a commotion

blocks.note: the shin is the front of the lower leg
a dig is an archaeological excavation

explanation.surface: An archaeologist's dig unearths a leg bone and stirs up excitement.
explanation.definitionFit: A shindig is a noisy, lively party or a rumpus, so it is a commotion.

clue.text: Decree cited incorrectly

indicators.note: something written incorrectly has its letters out of their proper order

blocks.note: letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: An official order was misquoted.
explanation.definitionFit: An edict is an official order issued by an authority, a synonym for decree.

clue.text: Smooth ale, specially brewed, is disgusting

indicators.note: something specially brewed has been mixed up from its ingredients, so these letters are recombined

blocks.note: letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A smooth special beer turns out to taste horrible.
explanation.definitionFit: Loathsome means causing hatred or revulsion, a synonym for disgusting.

clue.text: Non-commissioned types in old armoured vehicles surrounding German man

indicators.note: surrounding means enclosing, so one piece goes around another

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
tanks are armoured fighting vehicles
Herr is the German for Mr

explanation.surface: Ordinary soldiers riding in old tanks around a German.
explanation.definitionFit: Other ranks is the British military term for all soldiers who are not commissioned officers.

clue.text: Look closely at tailless animal kept for breeding

indicators.note: without a tail means the final letter is cut off

blocks.note: to study something is to examine it carefully

explanation.surface: Examine a tailless creature kept to produce young.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tailless animal' looks like one phrase, but 'tailless' works on the verb before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A stud is a male animal, typically a stallion, kept for breeding purposes.
